sections.skill: Protect financial accounts online with strong passwords, multifactor authentication, and safe habits

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security

choices.text: Rosa2008 used on every site
The word "password" with the number 1 added at the end
A long, random phrase used only for one account
Her pet's name and birthday

questions.correct_answer: A long, random phrase used only for one account
questions.intro: Strong passwords are long, unique to each account, and hard to guess. A password manager can create and store them.
questions.feedback: Length plus uniqueness makes passwords strong.

misconceptions.D: Easy to guess from social media

sources: CISA (Secure Our World: Use strong passwords): Recommends long, unique passwords or a password manager, and turning on multifactor authentication. (https://www.cisa.gov/secure-our-world/use-strong-passwords)

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security

choices.text: A faster login with no password at all
A stronger password that is generated for you
Encryption for public Wi-Fi
A second proof of identity

questions.intro: MFA requires something besides your password, such as a code from an app or a security key, so a stolen password alone is not enough.

misconceptions.B: Confuses MFA with a password manager

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: A 4-digit PIN has 10 choices for each digit. How many possible PINs are there?
questions.intro: Possible codes = choices per position raised to the number of positions. Longer codes are much harder to guess.
sources: CISA (Secure Our World: Use strong passwords): Recommends long, unique passwords or a password manager, and turning on multifactor authentication. (https://www.cisa.gov/secure-our-world/use-strong-passwords)

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: Rosa is on free public Wi-Fi at a café. Which is safest?

choices.text: Log in to her bank to check her balance quickly
Wait to bank on a trusted network
Share her screen with strangers
Turn off her phone's updates

questions.correct_answer: Wait to bank on a trusted network
questions.feedback: Avoid sensitive logins on public Wi-Fi or use a trusted connection.

questions.domain: Consumer Protection, Fraud, and Digital Security
questions.prompt: What is a SIM swap scam?

choices.text: Copying your contacts to a new phone
A text offering a free SIM upgrade
A virus that slows your phone
A thief moves your phone number to their device

questions.correct_answer: A thief moves your phone number to their device
questions.intro: With your number, a thief can receive text codes. Add a carrier PIN and prefer app-based or key-based MFA.
questions.feedback: SIM swaps hijack phone numbers to steal codes.
sources: CISA (Secure Our World: Use strong passwords): Recommends long, unique passwords or a password manager, and turning on multifactor authentication. (https://www.cisa.gov/secure-our-world/use-strong-passwords)
